title: Hound · nose and speed
blurb: Two very different hunting methods in one shelf: the scent hounds that follow a line on the ground, and the sighthounds that run what they see.

items.d: The scent hound of the monastery and the courtroom: loose skin, long ears and a nose that trails for days.
French low-slung scent hound, 30–38 cm, built to follow a line under cover with its nose to the ground.
Small English pack hound, 33–40 cm, bred to hunt hare and now the classic family scent dog.
German badger dog: long body, short legs and a courage that ignores its size.
Southern African hound with a ridge of reversed hair, bred to trail lions and guard the homestead.
The fastest dog, 70 km/h over a sprint; the oldest sighthound type, calm and thin-skinned at home.
The small English sighthound, 44–51 cm, quiet indoors and a 55 km/h runner in the field.
Russian wolfhound with a long silky coat, bred by the nobility to course wolves in open country.
